ORDERING, recorded because A1 demands the order and not only the content: this record's FIRST commit contains the five rows below together with the whole A2/A3/A4/A5/A15/A27 pre-edit baseline, and `git status --porcelain` at that commit showed ONLY .agents/v2/evidence/ paths -- internal/domain/pause_resume_test.go and internal/application/pause.go did not yet exist, and every other file named in allowed_paths was still byte-identical to the base commit. V2-087 produced this table's content only after its edits and had to report that as its one unmet item; V2-084, V2-088 and V2-089 did it in the right order; this task follows them. ROW 1 -- WHAT THIS TASK MAKES TRUE. An owner can pause a Requirement from ready, active, waiting or recovering; a paused Requirement remembers exactly which of those four it came from, in ONE new field domain.Requirement.PausedFrom; the owner can resume it into that same status and into no other, through ONE new command kind domain.RequirementResume admitted from domain.RequirementPaused only; the owner can cancel it; and a paused Requirement has at least one exit under every one of the seven control modes, because pause and cancel evaluate NO domain.Permit while resume evaluates domain.PermitClaim -- so under emergency-stop resume is DENIED and cancel is ALLOWED. The pausable status set is declared ONCE, as one unexported helper in internal/domain/model.go, and READ TWICE: by the pause branch's allowed(...) call and by the resume branch's guard, so resume's legal TARGETS are derived from pause's legal SOURCES rather than declared a second time. Three owner-only application commands live in ONE new file internal/application/pause.go; three POST routes (:pause, :resume, :cancel) join internal/api/api.go's POST default branch; one additive optional resumes_to field joins the requirement detail read model; three openapi paths and their schemas join contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml. ROW 2 -- WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. It propagates nothing to a Runner, terminates no Execution, expires no Lease, verifies no stop completion, writes no Control Intent (Service.PauseRequirement stages no control record and Service.Control transitions no Requirement -- re-measured at internal/application/service.go:1457, where the Work Order says :1307), stages no outbox item (every s.record call passes a NIL OutboxItem), adds no port (internal/application/ports.go is prohibited), adds no environment variable, changes nextAction by not one byte (re-measured at internal/application/readmodels.go:309-332: it branches on completed and cancelled and on Increment and Execution status and NEVER on paused), changes no existing response field, adds no RequirementStatus, and adds ZERO product text -- docs/** is PROHIBITED because every edge this task makes reachable is already described (A4). internal/application/service.go, internal/application/framing.go, internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go, internal/application/framing_test.go, internal/domain/source_guard_test.go, internal/domain/control.go, internal/store/**, internal/quota/**, ci/**, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are all PROHIBITED and all byte-unchanged. ROW 3 -- WHAT IT RECORDS BUT DOES NOT FIX. (a) The TWO CELLS where internal/domain's cancel branch is WIDER than the product table: docs/architecture/domain-model.md:270 lists recovering's 主な遷移先 as active, waiting, needs-input and paused with `cancelled` ABSENT, and :271 lists evaluating's as completed, active and needs-input with `cancelled` ABSENT, while internal/domain/model.go:515-519's cancel branch admits every status except completed and cancelled and therefore admits both. NOT narrowed, NOT asserted (A5). (b) nextAction has no paused branch, so a paused Requirement with a running Execution still reports 'monitor execution'. NOT fixed, NOT asserted (A16). (c) Service.Claim's parent check is V2-089's four-status admitting set, so a CANCELLED Requirement's Increments are now correctly refused, but Service.Plan and Service.Prepare still write the parent without consulting its status, so an Increment can still be PLANNED and PREPARED under a paused or cancelled Requirement -- V2-084's F1, partially closed by V2-089 and recorded here as the surviving half. (d) The six-rung ladder at docs/architecture/domain-model.md:336 names a `paused` rung that domain.controlSeverity (re-measured at internal/domain/control.go:112-128) implements as NO ControlMode: the severities are emergency-stop 7, immediate-stop and cancel 6, graceful-stop 5, pause-claim 3, pause-intake 2, allow 0 -- severity 4 is unoccupied and no ControlMode named `paused` exists. (e) internal/application/framing.go:113-117's comment still says 'Plan and Prepare evaluate no Permit at all', which V2-085 invalidated: re-measured, internal/application/service.go:984 evaluates domain.Permit with domain.PermitClaim inside Service.Plan. framing.go is prohibited; the stale comment is recorded, not repaired. ROW 4 -- WHAT ONLY A LATER TASK CAN ESTABLISH. That pausing actually STOPS running work, which needs the propagation half and the stop-completion observation docs/product/definition.md:164 defines (対象workerのack、process終了、lease解放または失効、新規副作用の不在まで観測して初めて停止完了とする). And that `waiting` and `recovering` can be pause-entered through a REAL journey, which needs non-test issuers for domain.RequirementWait and domain.RequirementRecover that this task does not add: re-measured, `grep -rn '\bRequirementWait\b' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go` and the same for RequirementRecover each return only internal/domain/model.go's declaration and switch case, so no journey can put a Requirement into either status. That is why A14's GRADE 3 (over HTTP) covers ready and active ONLY, and it is a LIMIT OF THIS TASK rather than a gap in the assertion: GRADE 1 (internal/domain, exhaustive) and GRADE 2 (internal/application over the real Service and a real store, by seeding) cover all four. ROW 5 -- RELEASE GATES. This task passes NO release gate on its own. release_eligible is false in all four index entries, no capability id is cited anywhere in any of the four records, and no live-provider evidence record is issued.
